short: The discerning, deciding faculty — the highest of the inner instruments.
beginner: Buddhi is the part of us that decides and understands — the faculty that can say 'this is right'. A clear, steady buddhi is what lets us act well instead of being pushed around by impulses.
what: In Sankhya, buddhi (also mahat, 'the great') is the first evolute of prakriti, the seat of ascertainment, and closest in clarity to purusha. The Gita repeatedly speaks of a resolute, single-pointed intellect (vyavasayatmika buddhi) versus a scattered one, and of buddhi yoga — the discipline of an even intellect. It also classifies intellect by the gunas.
scholar: Sankhya Karika 23 lists the sattvic and tamasic forms of buddhi (dharma, knowledge, dispassion, power and their opposites). In Nyaya, buddhi simply means cognition, a quality of the self — a different sense. Vedanta places buddhi in the subtle body, often as vijnanamaya kosha, the sheath of intellect in the Taittiriya scheme.

perspectives.view: Buddhi is the first product of prakriti, the faculty of determination; in it purusha's light is reflected, producing apparent consciousness.
Buddhi is the subtle instrument where the Self is most easily mistaken for the individual; purified, it reflects Self-knowledge.
Buddhi means cognition itself — a quality that arises in the self, not a separate faculty.

follow.note: A resolute intellect is one-pointed; the irresolute is many-branched.
Senses, mind, intellect and what lies beyond the intellect.
The sattvic intellect knows what to do and what not to do.
Buddhi as the first evolute of nature.
